comments.body:
Thanks for picking this up. I found no code defect at 6be4a4f, but the fix changes replay policy, so I'd like to settle that before merge. All checks pass, and there are no conflicts.

Returning `undefined` at [target-evidence.ts:164](https://github.com/callstack/agent-device/blob/6be4a4f/packages/selectors/src/target-evidence.ts#L164) turns a step the recorder cannot verify into an unannotated step. Replay refuses a recorded `unverifiable` annotation before dispatch (`target-verification.ts:109` and `:151`), but it runs a step with no annotation without any target check (`target-annotation.md:259`). So for an oversized label this replaces fail-closed with fail-open, while ADR 0012 says evidence that cannot isolate a target must be an identity-unverifiable divergence, never a silent pick.

#4354 fixes the same issue by keeping an `unverifiable` annotation and dropping optional fields until it fits, so replay still refuses. The two do not compose, so only one should land. Would you be open to that approach? If you prefer omission, the docs and ADR need to say that replay runs that step unguarded.

Not blocking: `finalizeOversizedCandidate` repeats the size check that `fitsPayloadCeiling` already holds, and a second test case where dropping the rect alone fits, and the result reparses with `parseTargetAnnotationV1Payload`, would pin the neighbouring behavior.

I read the code and computed the escaped payload size; I did not run the tests.

Thanks again for picking this up. #4354 has now merged with the fail-closed approach for #4333 (an over-limit annotation is downgraded and replay still refuses it), so this PR conflicts with main in `target-evidence.ts`, its test and the two docs, and its omission path is superseded. Unless you see a case #4354 misses, I think this one can be closed.
